title: Maximum Performance of a Team
description: Maximize speed-sum times minimum-efficiency for a team of at most k engineers, using an efficiency-descending sweep with a size-capped min-heap.

blocks.text: 1. Problem Statement

There are n engineers, each with a speed[i] and efficiency[i]. Choose at most k engineers to form a team maximizing the team's performance, defined as (sum of the chosen engineers' speeds) multiplied by (the minimum efficiency among the chosen engineers). Return the maximum performance modulo 10^9 + 7.

blocks.caption: Processing engineers from highest to lowest efficiency lets a min-heap of speeds evaluate every possible minimum-efficiency team.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Field","Details"],"rows":[["Input","speed[] and efficiency[] (both length n), k (max team size)"],["Performance formula","(sum of chosen speeds) * (minimum chosen efficiency)"],["Team size","At most k engineers, at least 1"],["Output","Maximum achievable performance, modulo 10^9 + 7"]]}

blocks.text: 2. Pattern Detection

The performance formula multiplies a SUM (speeds) by a MIN (efficiency). Whenever the minimum of a chosen set is one of the two factors, sorting by that quantity and processing in order lets each element take a turn being "the minimum," since a team's effective efficiency is always the last (smallest efficiency) member added when processing in descending efficiency order.

blocks.title: Connection
blocks.text: A min-heap that evicts the smallest speed once the team exceeds k members is the natural tool for maintaining "the k fastest engineers seen so far," a queue-like priority structure.
3. Understand the Problem

Picture a team captain assembling a roster of at most k players. Each player has a speed rating and a skill rating; the team's overall score is total speed times the WEAKEST skill rating on the team, since the team is only as strong as its weakest link. The captain wants to try every possible "weakest link" and, for that choice, keep only the fastest players whose skill is at least that strong.

blocks.caption: Each engineer, processed in efficiency order, gets a turn as the team's bottleneck skill.

items: If engineers are processed from highest to lowest efficiency, the current engineer is always the lowest-efficiency member of any team formed from itself plus previously processed engineers.
For that fixed minimum efficiency, the best team includes the current engineer plus the (k-1) fastest OTHER previously-seen engineers.
A min-heap of size at most k, keyed by speed, naturally maintains "the k fastest engineers with efficiency at least the current one."

blocks.text: 4. Understand with Examples
n = 6, speed = [2,10,3,1,5,8], efficiency = [5,4,3,9,7,2], k = 2. Sorted by efficiency descending: (eff=9,spd=1), (eff=7,spd=5), (eff=5,spd=2), (eff=4,spd=10), (eff=3,spd=3), (eff=2,spd=8).

blocks.title: Answer
blocks.text: The maximum performance is 60, achieved at efficiency 4 with the team of engineers having speeds 5 and 10 (total speed 15, times minimum efficiency 4 = 60), matching the expected output.
5. How Should We Think?
A brute-force approach tries every possible subset of size up to k, computing each subset's speed sum and minimum efficiency directly. This is correct but exponential, far too slow for realistic n.

Sorting by efficiency descending and processing one engineer at a time fixes the minimum-efficiency-so-far to exactly the current engineer's efficiency, since every LATER engineer processed will have equal or lower efficiency. This turns "try every possible minimum efficiency" into a single linear pass, with a min-heap efficiently maintaining the best (fastest) k-or-fewer engineers eligible at each step.
6. Brute Force Solution
Recursively enumerate every subset of size at most k, computing speed sum and minimum efficiency for each, tracking the best performance found.
7. Analyze the Brute Force

blocks.content: {"headers":["Metric","Value","Why"],"rows":[["Time","O(C(n, k) * k)","Enumerates every subset of size up to k, each costing O(k) to evaluate"],["Space","O(k)","Recursion depth and the chosen list"]]}

blocks.title: Bottleneck
blocks.text: The number of subsets grows combinatorially, making this infeasible for n up to 10^5 as in the actual constraints.
8. Optimize the Solution

Sort engineers by efficiency descending. Maintain a min-heap of speeds with at most k elements. For each engineer in order, add their speed to the heap and to a running speed sum; if the heap now exceeds k elements, evict the smallest speed (subtracting it from the running sum), since that engineer is no longer among the k fastest available at this efficiency level. After each insertion/eviction, compute speedSum * currentEfficiency and update the best answer.

items: Sort by efficiency descending, O(n log n).
Maintain a min-heap of speeds capped at size k, each insertion/eviction O(log k).
The current engineer's efficiency is always the true minimum for any team formed from the heap's current contents, since all later engineers have equal or lower efficiency.

blocks.text: 9. Optimized Solution

codes.python:
import heapq


def max_performance(n, speed, efficiency, k):
    MOD = 10 ** 9 + 7
    engineers = sorted(zip(efficiency, speed), reverse=True)

    heap = []
    speed_sum = 0
    best = 0

    for eff, spd in engineers:
        heapq.heappush(heap, spd)
        speed_sum += spd
        if len(heap) > k:
            speed_sum -= heapq.heappop(heap)
        best = max(best, speed_sum * eff)

    return best % MOD


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(max_performance(6, [2, 10, 3, 1, 5, 8], [5, 4, 3, 9, 7, 2], 2))
    print(max_performance(6, [2, 10, 3, 1, 5, 8], [5, 4, 3, 9, 7, 2], 3))

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","Time","Space"],"rows":[["Brute Force, subset enumeration","O(C(n, k) * k)","O(k)"],["Optimized, sort + min-heap","O(n log n)","O(n)"]]}

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: When a formula multiplies a sum by a minimum, sort by the "minimum" quantity descending so each element takes exactly one turn as the effective minimum.
A min-heap capped at size k is the standard way to maintain "the k best (here, fastest) eligible items seen so far."
This sort-then-heap pattern generalizes to any "maximize sum times bottleneck" optimization problem.

blocks.text: 12. Final Summary

Maximum Performance of a Team is solved by sorting engineers by efficiency descending, so each engineer in turn represents the true minimum efficiency of any team formed so far, then maintaining a size-k min-heap of speeds to always keep the fastest eligible engineers. This turns an exponential subset search into an O(n log n) sort-and-heap sweep.
